verdict.stance: Overweight / Improving SA Tier-1 Bank Capital & Credit Quality
verdict.summary: South Africa Tier-1 peer to Standard Bank & FirstRand: H126 headline earnings rose 8% YoY to R12.8bn (15.0% ROE) with CET1 strengthening to 12.8% (above 11.0-12.5% board target) and Total CAR 16.1%. Credit loss ratio compressed to 88bp in FY25; Fitch lifted national scale to AAA(zaf) in mid-2026.

positives: Capital at top of target band: H126 CET1 12.8% (vs 11.0-12.5% target) and Total CAR 16.1%.
Credit quality recovery: Credit loss ratio improved from 103bp (FY24) to 88bp (FY25) and remained resilient in H126.
Pan-African diversification and active international Tier 2 market access (Dec-25 $150m & 6.625% 2036 USD Tier 2).
negatives: South Africa sovereign rating cap (Ba2/BB-) limits international USD rating upside.
Pan-African Rest-of-Africa subsidiaries face rate cuts and FX translation headwinds.
Competitive domestic deposit pricing dampening net interest margin expansion.

background.business_overview: One of South Africa's 'Big Four' universal banks (R2.28tn assets) operating across SA retail/business/CIB and 12 African markets.
background.asset_perimeter: Absa Bank South Africa + Absa Regional Operations (ARO across East/West/Southern Africa).
background.ownership_governance: JSE-listed (ABG); South African Reserve Bank (PA) supervised.

recent_drivers: H1 2026 Interim Results: Headline earnings R12.8bn (+8% YoY), revenue R58.8bn (+4% YoY), assets R2.28tn, CET1 12.8%, CAR 16.1%, ROE 15.0%.
Capital Markets & Rating: Fitch lifted national scale to AAA(zaf) mid-2026; issued $150m Tier 2 (Dec-25) and USD 6.625% Tier 2 due Jun-36.

catalysts.impact: Confirms full-year credit loss ratio inside target and ARO FX drag.

management_questions.question: Assess Rest-of-Africa sovereign exposure (Ghana/Kenya/Zambia/Mozambique) and local-currency capital repatriation.
